local_facts.claim: The North Carolina Utilities Commission regulates household-goods transportation within North Carolina. A mover needs a Commission certificate for intrastate household-goods transportation and must follow the Maximum Rate Tariff.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A Raleigh move that stays in North Carolina should have an identifiable authorized mover, written paperwork, and the consumer information required by the Commission. A move that crosses a state line needs its own operating plan rather than an assumption that the intrastate rules apply.
local_facts.title: North Carolina keeps household-goods moves under Utilities Commission oversight

local_facts.claim: Raleigh Right-of-Way Services says parking passes for moving vans can be obtained directly from Raleigh Parking; for timed or paid spaces, the approved pass must be displayed while the space is occupied.
local_facts.why_it_matters: For downtown or other paid-curb moves, the truck location should be confirmed before moving day. It reduces the risk that a crew arrives without a legal place to stand or has to make a long carry from an available space.
local_facts.title: A downtown truck space may need a Raleigh Parking pass

local_facts.claim: NC State University Housing scheduled its fall 2026 move-in operation for August 13–15 and tells residents to select a move-in appointment time slot.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A move to university housing has a defined arrival window instead of open-ended curb access. The crew, vehicle, inventory, and building access need to be matched to the assigned appointment before the job is scheduled.
local_facts.title: Campus move-in runs on appointments, not an open curb

pricing.table_head: What Raleigh movers post, under a state rate ceiling

anchors.label: State maximum, truck and two movers, regular hours
anchors.detail: Maximum Rate Tariff No. 2 took effect January 1, 2026 and caps an hourly intrastate household move of fifty miles or less. Regular time runs 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, and the clock starts when the crew arrives at the origin.
anchors.source_name: North Carolina Utilities Commission Maximum Rate Tariff No. 2

anchors.label: Same tariff, four movers after hours
anchors.detail: Overtime maximums run higher across the board: $235.15 for a truck and two, $310.25 for three, $385.15 for four. Each extra crew member adds $74.85 an hour and each extra vehicle $65.75.
anchors.source_name: Maximum Rate Tariff No. 2, Rule 53 hourly rates

anchors.label: Full value protection, tariff price
anchors.detail: Item 18 sets full value protection at a dollar per hundred dollars of declared value on a single-truck shipment, with a five dollar per pound minimum valuation. Released value at sixty cents a pound is the default and it is not insurance.

anchors.label: Median hourly wage, freight and material movers, Raleigh-Cary
anchors.detail: The May 2025 median across 17,060 workers in the metro. It is the floor the tariff ceiling sits above, and the gap between the two is where trucks, fuel, insurance and dispatch live.
anchors.source_name: BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2025

rows.note: Every posted figure in this market sits under the tariff ceiling for the same crew, some of them well under it.
